mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue expectations for S&P 500 constituents and results in negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that rises by more than 0.4 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in more than 80% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% in the same month signals a stagflationary shock, which increases both discount rates and cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such stagflation months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of more than 10% over six months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of such housing recovery periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a mixed labor market signal, often preceding a slowdown, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such mixed labor market months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% over four consecutive months signals weakening consumer spending, which reduces revenue growth for S&P 500 firms and results in negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in more than 80% of such persistent retail sales decline episodes.
